speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, could you describe any specific symptoms you're experiencing, such as pain, blood in urine, or fever? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the color or smell of your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the relief of symptoms with voiding and dyspareunia are significant clues. Have you noticed any urgency, nocturia worsening over time, or any pelvic pressure or a palpable mass? Additionally, have you ever been diagnosed with interstitial cystitis or undergone any gynecological procedures?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS). The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency, nocturia, and dyspareunia in the absence of urinary tract infection or pelvic mass is classic for this condition. I recommend a urine culture to definitively rule out infection and a cystoscopy with hydrodistension if symptoms persist despite conservative management.
